> The global celebration of the Ghana 70th Platinum Jubilee, held in London, 5 to 7 March 2027. Official site: https://ghanaat70uk.com

## Ghana at 70
In honour of seventy years of Ghanaian independence. Three days in London, 5 to 7 March 2027.
Take your seat at the Jubilee Discover the three events
Until Independence Day

In honour of
## Seventy years since Ghana became free.
On 6 March 1957, Ghana declared its independence. On 6 March 2027 it reaches its Platinum Jubilee, and London gathers to honour it.
6 March 1957 The nation At midnight Ghana became free and independent, the Black Star that lit the way for a continent.
Seventy years The people The generations who built Ghana, and the Ghanaians whose lives have enriched Britain for centuries.
Today The friendship Between Ghana and the United Kingdom, and everyone, of every heritage, who loves Ghana.
An independent celebration, organised by Ghana at 70 UK and open to everyone.
Choose your event
## Where will you be when Ghana turns 70?
Three occasions, each complete in itself. Choose one, or come to all three.

Partner spotlight
## The partners behind the celebration.
Creative Partner
## TwinsDntBeg, leading the Creative Hub
Twin brothers Emmanuel and Samuel Appiah Gyan are the Ghanaian photography and film duo behind Swag of Africa Studios. In November 2026 they announced a collaboration with Canon to develop the next generation of African photographers, filmmakers and creators. Their work with Rocky Dawuni on Rise was nominated for Music Film of the Year at the 2025 Black Stars International Film Festival. They curate Seventy Years in Frame: seventy photographs, a film of seven decades and the Creative Showcase on Independence Day.
Seventy Years in Frame Visit TwinsDntBeg
Fashion Partner Ghana
## Quophi Akotuah, leading the Fashion Show
A luxury fashion house founded in Accra in 2015 by Michael Addo, known as Quophi Michaels, and crowned King of the Glitz Style Awards in 2017. Quophi Akotuah leads the team of Ghanaian fashion houses joining us in London for the Ghana at 70 Fashion Show, open to every house, and offers guests a ticket holder price on made to measure outfits, with a final fitting in London.
The Fashion Show Visit Quophi Akotuah
Partner
## Impact Africa, leading the Business Hub
Impact Africa is a UK to Africa business, investment and market access platform, founded by Kwabena Anoff. Through its business accelerator, Africa investment roadshows and the annual Impact Africa Business and Investment Summit, it connects founders with capital, markets and partners. Impact Africa is a partner of Ghana at 70 UK, and Kwabena Anoff leads the Business Hub at the Ghana Day Festival.
Visit Impact Africa
All our partners · Become a partner
Our signature
## We have done this before.
Dignitaries in Kente and gold. A live saxophone. Every guest looked after.
Our signature. The opening of the Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East, produced by the Ghana at 70 UK team.
Friday 5 to Sunday 7 March 2027 · The setting
## Banking Hall, City of London.
Grade II listed marble, moments from the Bank of England. For one weekend, it belongs to Ghana.
See the hall
Seventy years · One family
## The Motherland is us.
Somewhere in Barking tonight, a mother is ironing a Kente cloth she has kept for thirty years.
She wore it the day she landed. She wore it to every wedding, every outdooring and every graduation. On the fifth of March she will wear it again.
Continue the story
In Manchester, a young man is choosing a Black Stars shirt. In Birmingham, two aunties are already arguing about whose jollof is best. In Glasgow, a student is booking the train south. In Dublin, a family is booking the flight over. In Amsterdam and Hamburg, cousins are comparing flights. In New York, Houston and Toronto, an uncle has already booked. Some of us were born in Osu, some in Kumasi, some in Leeds and others in south London, and every one of us knows the words of that midnight in 1957: Ghana, your beloved country, is free forever.
On 6 March 1957 our grandparents danced until morning. Now it is our turn. From every corner of the UK, from Europe, from North America and from Ghana itself, Ghanaians are coming together in one great hall for three days: The Royal Jubilee Gala on Independence Eve, the Ghana Day Festival on Independence Day itself, and Women of the Motherland on Mothering Sunday.
Red for those who gave their lives for freedom. Gold for the wealth of the land. Green for its forests and fields. And the Black Star, the lodestar of African freedom. Seventy years on, we honour every colour of the flag.
Ghana is seventy. Ghana is ours. Come and celebrate Ghana.
Take your seat at the Jubilee Read our story
An open invitation
To every friend of Ghana
## Come and celebrate with us.
Whether Ghana is your heritage, your second home or simply a place you have come to love, you are warmly invited. Join us in London as Ghana celebrates seventy years of independence.

## The Royal Jubilee Gala
Independence Eve. Fontomfrom drums at the door, dinner carried to the long tables, highlife until late, and the whole hall on its feet at midnight.
Black Tie, ball gown or Kente Banking Hall, City of London GBP 200 · first release GBP 150 Long tables A separate event, with its own ticket Book now Add to calendar Share with family
Independence Eve
## Midnight, 6 March. Seventy years free.
In 1957 our grandparents stood under the warm night sky of Accra and waited for midnight.
On Independence Eve we wait for it together again, in Kente and gold, with guests from every corner of the UK, Europe, North America and Ghana, in a grand banking hall in the City of London.
Continue the story
Fontomfrom drums at the door. A Ghanaian inspired dinner at long tables. Live highlife and a dance floor. Then, as the clock turns, the whole hall rises, glasses high, for the moment Ghana became free, seventy years on.
Arrive in your finest. One night, seventy years in the making.
Take your seat at the Jubilee The Royal Jubilee Gala Fri 5 March · 18:30 · GBP 200 · first release GBP 150 Book now
The setting
## Banking Hall, City of London.
A Grade II listed Art Deco banking hall on Cornhill, moments from the Bank of England and the Royal Exchange. For one night, the grandest dining room in the City belongs to Ghana.
Banking Hall dressed in Kente and gold for the Royal Jubilee Gala.
Address 14 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND
Heritage Grade II listed 1930s Art Deco, once a Lloyds Bank headquarters
The room A seated dinner at long tables
Nearest station Bank, about two minutes on foot
Getting there Bank Central, Northern, Waterloo and City lines and the DLR, about two minutes on foot. Monument District and Circle lines. Mainline rail Cannon Street, Fenchurch Street and Liverpool Street, with the Elizabeth line at Liverpool Street.
Dressed for Independence Eve
The Main Hall Black and gold Down the hall At the staircase The Main Hall Black and gold Down the hall At the staircase
For those who came before us. For those who walk beside us. For those who will follow.

## Received with protocol.
Ministers, diplomats, traditional leaders and the heads of institutions, banks and businesses are received as the occasion deserves.
A dedicated host Each delegation is met at the door and accompanied throughout the evening.
Seating by precedence Tables for official guests are arranged with your office in advance.
Arrival and departure A booked drop off on Cornhill and a quiet route into the hall, agreed beforehand.
Titles and forms of address Confirmed with your office for name cards, the table plan and any announcement.
One point of contact Protocol is arranged directly with your office. Official enquiries

Before you book Is everything confirmed?
Yes. All three days are at Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, in the City of London, moments from the Bank of England. If we ever cancel, every ticket is refunded in full within 14 days. It is in our terms.
Who is behind it?
The team that produced the opening of the Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. Watch the film .
Is this the Ghana Independence dinner and dance in London?
Yes. The Royal Jubilee Gala is the black tie dinner dance on the eve of Ghana Independence Day: a Ghanaian inspired dinner, a live band playing highlife and Afrobeats, the dance floor until the last dance, and the midnight toast as 6 March 2027 begins.
What do I wear?
Black tie and ball gowns, with Kente welcome. This is a ball. What to wear
Can I book a table for my group?
Yes. A table of ten is GBP 1,800: ten guests seated together at the long tables, for the price of nine: 9 x GBP 200. Choose Table of ten when you book.
Is the programme confirmed?
The programme shown is the plan we are building to. Performers, speakers and timings are announced as each one is contracted, and every booked guest hears first.
Every other question
Continue the weekend

Saturday 6 March 2027 · 08:30 to 17:00 Seventy years to the day
## Ghana Day Festival
Independence Day, seventy years to the day. A day of trade, capital and celebration, under one roof.
Book Exhibit with us Add to calendar Share with family Ghana Day Festival Sat 6 March · 08:30 · GBP 50 Book now
Saturday 6 March 2027 · 08:30 to 17:00
## Four worlds. One day.
08:30 to 17:00 The Creative Hub Led by TwinsDntBeg Seventy Years in Frame, the Creative Showcase at 13:00 and Ghana on Screen at 15:00. Funtunfunefu Denkyemfunefu, the two crocodiles that share one stomach. Two minds, one purpose.
14:00 The Fashion Show Led by Quophi Akotuah Ghanaian couture on the runway. Adinkrahene, the chief of symbols. Greatness and charisma.
08:30 to 14:00 The Business Hub Led by Kwabena Anoff, Impact Africa Ten minute meetings, by appointment, in the Counting Room. Nkonsonkonson, the chain link. Strength in connection.
09:00 to 17:00 The Exhibition The marketplace Every kind of business, in the Main Hall. Fawohodie, independence. Seventy years of it.
At 11:00, the drums. Then the DJ, until five.
Exhibitors · Saturday 6 March 2027

# Page: https://ghanaat70uk.com/women-of-the-motherland
Sunday 7 March 2027 · Mothering Sunday · 11:00 to 18:30 Rooted and Rising
## Women of the Motherland
Mothering Sunday, the day after Independence Day. An afternoon in honour of the women who carried us, with the family she raised around her.
Family afternoon tea The Wall of Mothers A family portrait The whole family All ages welcome Register your interest GBP 150 A separate event, with its own ticket Book now Add to calendar Share with family
Mothering Sunday
## Bring your mother. She brought you here.
She ironed the cloth. She sent money home on Friday and still had Sunday dinner on the table.
Some of our mothers live around the corner. Some came down from Manchester or up from Kent for the day. Some are at home in Ghana, waiting for the photographs.
Continue the story
On Mothering Sunday, the day after Independence Day, we honour them all: a family afternoon tea, a family portrait, and the Wall of Mothers, where every mother named by a guest is celebrated aloud.
Our symbol, Akoko Nan, is a mother who shelters and corrects her children, and never lets go. This is her day.
Book her seat at the table Women of the Motherland Sun 7 March · 11:00 · GBP 150 Book now
Daughters of the Motherland
## Formidable, and this Sunday is hers.
Seven on a Sunday morning in Barking. Payroll signed, her mother called from Kumasi, Lagos or Harare, her finest wrapper pressed for church.
She built careers, homes and whole communities. She is rarely celebrated in a room built for her.
On Mothering Sunday, the day after Ghana turns seventy, Ghana opens its doors to every woman, whatever her heritage. A family afternoon tea, at Banking Hall.
The women who carried us. The women who believed in us. The women who made a way when there seemed to be no way.
Mothering Sunday afternoon
## An afternoon worthy of her.
Tea, her family around her, and her name read aloud.

Real support, beyond the day
## The Resource Village.
Trusted support partners, open throughout the afternoon. Speak privately, take information home, and leave knowing exactly where to turn.
Health
Health information for women, wellbeing checks and screening guidance
Legal
Wills, family matters and property in Britain and back home
Money
Pensions, savings and financial guidance
Safety
Confidential signposting for anyone facing abuse at home
Community
Faith groups, networks and mentoring for women
The Village and the Motherland Market sit in the two side aisles, so every family keeps its table. Support partners will be announced from January 2027. Organisations serving women can apply to join the Village , and brands can register their interest .
The Motherland Toolkit A printed guide every guest takes home.
A health checklist for every decade
A money and wills checklist for Britain and back home
A directory of support organisations and helplines
Your pledge card and the Sister Circle details
If you or someone you know is affected by abuse at home, the National Domestic Abuse Helpline is open 24 hours on 0808 2000 247.

# Page: https://ghanaat70uk.com/ghana-at-70
Saturday 6 March 2027 · The 70th anniversary
## Ghana at 70.
Saturday 6 March 2027 marks seventy years since the Gold Coast became Ghana at midnight on 6 March 1957. It is the Platinum Jubilee of Independence, and everyone who loves Ghana, from across the world, celebrates it together in London, 5 to 7 March 2027.
Independence Day 2027 6 March 1957 Seventy years Ghana and Britain In London Questions Book The three days
Key facts
## Ghana Independence Day 2027, at a glance.
Date
Saturday 6 March 2027
Anniversary
The 70th, a Platinum Jubilee
Independence
Midnight, 6 March 1957, at the Old Polo Grounds in Accra
Before 1957
The British colony of the Gold Coast
First leader
Kwame Nkrumah, Prime Minister in 1957 and the first President when Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960
The flag
Red, gold and green with a Black Star, designed by Theodosia Okoh. Her story and the meaning of the colours
National motto
Freedom and Justice
In Ghana
A public holiday
In the UK
Not a public holiday. Ghana at 70 UK marks it over three days in London, 5 to 7 March 2027
6 March 1957 · Accra
## Midnight in Accra.
At midnight, before a vast crowd at the Old Polo Grounds, Kwame Nkrumah declared the Gold Coast free. The new nation took the name Ghana, after the ancient Ghana Empire of West Africa.
Ghana was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule, and within a decade most of the continent had followed.
“Ghana, your beloved country, is free forever.”
The midnight toast
Seventy years
## Why seventy is a Platinum Jubilee.
Twenty five years is a silver jubilee, fifty a golden jubilee and sixty a diamond jubilee. Seventy is platinum, the rarest of them all.
Ghana marked the Golden Jubilee in 2007 as Ghana at 50. On 6 March 2027 Ghana reaches the Platinum Jubilee, and London is gathering to mark it, with everyone welcome.
The timeline
## Seventy years, in the moments that made a nation.
1947
## The United Gold Coast Convention
J. B. Danquah and others found the United Gold Coast Convention to campaign for self government. Kwame Nkrumah returns from London to become its general secretary.
1948
## The Christiansborg Crossroads
On 28 February, ex servicemen who fought for Britain in the Second World War march to present a petition. Shots are fired at the crossroads, unrest follows, and the Big Six are arrested.
1949
## The Convention Peoples Party
Nkrumah founds the Convention Peoples Party with a simple call: self government now.
1951
## From prison to power
The Convention Peoples Party wins the general election. Nkrumah is released from prison to lead the government, and becomes Prime Minister in 1952.
1957
## Independence
At midnight on 6 March, at the Old Polo Grounds in Accra, the Gold Coast becomes Ghana. Days later, Ghana joins the United Nations.
1960
## The Republic
On 1 July, Ghana becomes a republic, with Kwame Nkrumah as the first President.
1963
## African unity
Ghana helps found the Organisation of African Unity in Addis Ababa, the forerunner of the African Union.
1966
## Lake Volta
The Akosombo Dam opens, creating Lake Volta, one of the largest man made lakes in the world, and power for the nation.
1966 to 1992
## Years of change
Ghana passes through military and civilian governments, before a new constitution is approved by referendum in 1992.
1993
## The Fourth Republic
On 7 January the Fourth Republic begins: a democracy in which power has since changed hands peacefully at the ballot box.
1997
## Kofi Annan
Born in Kumasi, Kofi Annan becomes Secretary General of the United Nations, the first from sub-Saharan Africa. He shares the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001.
2007
## Ghana at 50
The Golden Jubilee. Ghanaians at home and abroad mark fifty years of independence.
2010
## The Black Stars
Ghana reaches the quarter finals of the FIFA World Cup in South Africa, carrying the hopes of a continent. The same year, oil flows from the Jubilee Field.
2019
## The Year of Return
Four hundred years after the first enslaved Africans were recorded arriving in Virginia, Ghana invites the diaspora home.
2026
## Theodosia Okoh honoured
A new GHS 50 note honours Theodosia Okoh, who designed the national flag in 1957.
2027
## The Platinum Jubilee
On 6 March, Ghana is seventy. The world celebrates Ghana in London at Ghana at 70 UK , 5 to 7 March 2027.
Traditions
## How Ghanaians celebrate Independence Day.
In Ghana
## The parade
Traditionally, a national parade at Black Star Square in Accra, with schoolchildren, the security services and the President taking the salute, and celebrations in every region.
At home
## Family and food
Flags at the window, Kente and print, jollof, waakye and kelewele, highlife on the speaker and the whole family together.
Abroad
## Dinner and dance
Ghanaians across the diaspora mark the day with church services, flag raisings, dinner dances and community gatherings.
In 2027
## Ghana at 70 UK
Three days in London for everyone who loves Ghana, from across the world.
Ghana and Britain
## More than 250 years of Ghanaian life in Britain.
From Philip Quaque, ordained in the Church of England in 1765, to Arthur Wharton, the first Black professional footballer in the world, Ghanaians have shaped British life for more than two and a half centuries. Read our diaspora story .
Today Ghanaian families live in every part of the UK, from Milton Keynes, Birmingham and Manchester to Glasgow, Cardiff, Belfast and London. In March 2027 they come together, with guests from Europe, the Americas and Ghana, for the Platinum Jubilee.
5 to 7 March 2027 · Banking Hall, City of London
## Ghana Independence Day 2027 in London.
Three events, each with its own ticket, at Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, moments from the Bank of England.
Friday 5 March
## The Royal Jubilee Gala
Independence Eve. Black tie, ball gown or Kente, a Ghanaian inspired dinner, live highlife and the midnight toast. 18:30 to 00:30. GBP 200. See the Gala
Saturday 6 March
## Ghana Day Festival
Independence Day itself. The art, the exhibition, the drums at 11:00 and the Fashion Show. 08:30 to 17:00. GBP 50. See Ghana Day
Sunday 7 March
## Women of the Motherland
Mothering Sunday. Afternoon tea, the Wall of Mothers and a family portrait, for every woman and her family. GBP 150. See Sunday
Book your tickets Coming from further away
Quick answers
## Questions people ask
When is Ghana Independence Day 2027?
Saturday 6 March 2027, the 70th anniversary of independence.
What does Ghana at 70 mean?
Ghana at 70 marks seventy years of Ghanaian independence, from 6 March 1957 to 6 March 2027, the Platinum Jubilee. Ghana at 70 UK is the celebration of that jubilee in London, 5 to 7 March 2027.
Is Ghana Independence Day a public holiday in the UK?
No. It is a public holiday in Ghana. In 2027 it falls on a Saturday, so families in the UK can celebrate together on the day itself.
Where can I celebrate Ghana Independence Day in London in 2027?
At Ghana at 70 UK, Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND. The Ghana Day Festival runs on Independence Day itself, 08:30 to 17:00, GBP 50. The Royal Jubilee Gala is on the eve, Friday 5 March, GBP 200.
Who led Ghana to independence?
Kwame Nkrumah and the Convention Peoples Party, building on the campaign of the United Gold Coast Convention and the leaders remembered as the Big Six. Nkrumah was Prime Minister in 1957 and the first President when Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960.
What was Ghana called before independence?
The Gold Coast, a British colony. The name Ghana comes from the ancient Ghana Empire of West Africa.
Who designed the flag of Ghana?
Theodosia Okoh, in 1957. Red, gold and green, with a Black Star at the centre.
When was Ghana at 50?
In 2007, the Golden Jubilee. 2027 is the Platinum Jubilee, seventy years.
What should I wear to celebrate?
Kente, print or the colours of the flag. At Ghana at 70 UK: Black Tie, ball gown or Kente on Friday, print and denim or a Black Stars shirt on Saturday, and Sunday best on Sunday.
Can I come from outside the UK?
Yes. Guests are travelling from across Europe, the Americas and Ghana. Visitors from the EU, the USA and Canada need an Electronic Travel Authorisation before they travel, and visitors from Ghana need a UK visitor visa.

Saturday 6 March 2027 · Seventy years to the day
## Ghana Independence Day in London.
The Ghana Independence Day celebration in London for 2027 is the Ghana Day Festival: Saturday 6 March 2027, 08:30 to 17:00, at Banking Hall, City of London. The night before, the Royal Jubilee Gala raises the midnight toast.

The day
## Seventy years to the day.
At 11:00 the whole hall stops for the drums and a reading of the declaration of independence. Then the music starts again.
Across the day: the exhibition of companies of every kind, private 10 minute appointments, the Creative Showcase, the runway, Ghana on Screen and a DJ from 11:00.
Drinks and snacks are sold at the bar, by card. Food stalls sell sealed products to take home.
The night before
## Midnight, 6 March.
On Independence Eve, the Royal Jubilee Gala gathers guests in Black tie, ball gown or Kente for a Ghanaian inspired dinner, live highlife and dancing. As the clock turns to 6 March, the hall rises for the midnight toast, the very hour Ghana became free in 1957.
Make it the full weekend: Independence Day at the Ghana Day Festival , and close on Mothering Sunday at Women of the Motherland .
Quick answers
## Questions people ask
Where is the Ghana Independence Day celebration in London in 2027?
At Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND, on Saturday 6 March 2027, 08:30 to 17:00: the Ghana Day Festival by Ghana at 70 UK.
Is there a Ghana Independence evening event in London?
Yes. The Royal Jubilee Gala on the eve, Friday 5 March 2027, 18:30 to 00:30, ends with the midnight toast as Independence Day begins. GBP 200 per guest.
Is the Independence Day festival family friendly?
Yes. All ages are welcome, and every guest holds their own ticket.
Can I come and go during the day?
Yes. Your wristband lets you come and go between 08:30 and 17:00.
I live in Manchester, Birmingham or Milton Keynes. How do I get there?
Trains run to Euston, and the Northern line takes you to Bank in about 10 minutes. See journey times .
What should I wear?
Print and denim, a Black Stars shirt, Kente or the colours of the flag: red, gold and green.

Our 2027 theme
## The Platinum Jubilee.
Seventy years of Ghana, kept the way great jubilees are kept: with ceremony, splendour and the whole family in the room.
The idea The palette Across three days A touch of platinum For partners and exhibitors Questions Book The three days
The idea
## Platinum, for seventy years.
Every great anniversary has its metal. Silver for twenty five years, gold for fifty, diamond for sixty. Seventy years is platinum: the rarest and most enduring of them all.
On 6 March 2027 Ghana reaches its Platinum Jubilee, seventy years as the first nation of sub Saharan Africa to win its independence. We mark it in London as jubilees deserve to be marked: a grand hall, a red carpet, a long table, a midnight toast and three days of ceremony and joy.
Our theme brings two traditions together. The polish and pageantry of a platinum jubilee, and the cloth, drums and colour of Ghana. Platinum and gold, laid on Motherland green.
Book your place What is a platinum jubilee?
70 Platinum Jubilee 1957 · 2027
6 March 1957
## The Black Star of Africa.
The first nation of sub Saharan Africa to win its independence. Seventy years on, its people gather in London.
The precedent
## Kept the way jubilees are kept.
In June 2022 Britain marked the first platinum jubilee in its history, seventy years of the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, over a four day weekend. Every element had a meaning. Ours does too.
Element The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027
The emblem A platinum crown above the number 70, designed by a 19 year old student from Nottinghamshire. Our seal, Akoko Nan in gold, the mother who protects, beside the gold 70 and the Black Star.
The light More than 3,500 beacons lit across the UK and, for the first time, in every Commonwealth capital. The midnight toast, as 5 March becomes 6 March, the moment Ghana became free.
Thanksgiving A Service of Thanksgiving at St Pauls Cathedral, in the City of London. At 11:00 on 6 March, the drums and a reading of the declaration of independence, a short walk from St Pauls.
The evening The Platinum Party at the Palace. The Royal Jubilee Gala, a Ghanaian inspired dinner and a ball at Banking Hall.
The people The Big Jubilee Lunch, with some 16,000 street parties across the country. The Ghana Day Festival, the whole community in one hall on Independence Day.
The pageant Around 5,000 performers and a River of Hope of more than 200 silk flags. The runway, the drums and Kente in every colour of the flag.
The legacy The Queens Green Canopy, more than a million trees planted for future generations. The Heritage Wall, the true stories of Ghanaians in Britain since 1555, and Mothering Sunday for the women who carried us.
Figures for June 2022 from the published records of the Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II.
The palette
## Five colours. One story.
Platinum for the jubilee. Red, gold, green and the Black Star for the flag designed by Theodosia Okoh in 1957.
Platinum #E5E4E2 Seventy years. The rarest metal, for the rarest milestone.
Jubilee gold #D4A62A The wealth of the land, and the gold of the flag.
Motherland green #0A3523 Forests and fields, and the ground of every room.
Flag red #CE1126 For those who gave their lives for freedom.
Black Star #16201B The lodestar of African freedom.

Getting there
## Bank station, Exit 4. Then one minute on foot.
All three days are at Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND, on Bank Junction in the City of London.
Address Banking Hall 14 Cornhill London EC3V 3ND
Nearest station Bank Central, Northern, Waterloo and City lines and the DLR
Best exit Exit 4, Cornhill Exit 3, Royal Exchange, also works
Sat nav EC3V 3ND No parking at the venue
Open in Google Maps Open in Apple Maps Open in Citymapper
Every route, step by step
## From Bank station, in four steps
Follow the signs to Exit 4 On the platform signs it reads Exit 4: Cornhill, Leadenhall Market, Lloyds. Exit 3, Royal Exchange, brings you up just as close.
Come up on Bank Junction The great columned front of the Royal Exchange and the Bank of England stand around you.
Find Cornhill It is the street running between the Royal Exchange and the domed corner building at Number 1 Cornhill.
Walk a few doors along Banking Hall is at Number 14, on the side opposite the Royal Exchange. Our hosts in green and gold meet you at the door.
Not to scale. For live walking directions, open the address in your maps app.
Your route
## Wherever you are starting from.
By Underground
Bank Central, Northern and Waterloo and City lines and the DLR. Exit 4, then one minute on foot.
Monument District and Circle lines. Walk up King William Street to Bank Junction and turn right into Cornhill. About six minutes.
Waterloo and City line Waterloo to Bank in about four minutes. It runs Monday to Friday only, so it serves the Gala but not the weekend.
From a London terminal
Euston, Kings Cross, St Pancras Northern line, Bank branch, direct to Bank. About 10 minutes.
London Bridge Northern line, one stop to Bank.
Liverpool Street Central line, one stop to Bank, or about 10 minutes on foot along Bishopsgate and Cornhill.
Paddington Elizabeth line to Liverpool Street, then as above.
Cannon Street and Fenchurch Street About six to eight minutes on foot.
From the airports
London City DLR direct to Bank. About 25 minutes.
Heathrow Elizabeth line to Liverpool Street, then the Central line one stop to Bank.
Gatwick Thameslink to London Bridge, then the Northern line one stop to Bank.
Stansted Stansted Express to Liverpool Street, then the Central line one stop to Bank.
Eurostar St Pancras, then the Northern line direct to Bank.
By taxi or car
Taxi Ask for Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill. On weekdays Bank Junction is open to buses and cycles only during the day, so ask your driver to come along Cornhill from the Gracechurch Street end.
Parking The venue has none and City parking is scarce. Book a space in advance through a parking app.
Charges The venue is inside the Congestion Charge zone and the ULEZ. Check the hours on the TfL website before you drive.
Going home after the Gala
Night Tube On Friday night the Central line runs all night through Bank. The Northern line Night Tube runs on the Charing Cross branch, not through Bank.
Night buses Many routes serve Bank through the night.
Taxis Our hosts will point you to the pick up point on Cornhill as the evening closes.
Step free
Bank station Lifts from the Cannon Street entrance give step free access from street to train on the Northern line, the DLR and the Waterloo and City line. About five minutes on foot to Cornhill.
Inside Banking Hall The event is held over two floors joined by stairs. Read the access guide before you book.
For any journey, the TfL journey planner shows live times on the day.
Before you travel
## What you need to enter the UK.
It depends on the passport you travel on, not where you live. Every traveller, children included, needs their own.
Download the visa and ETA checklist
Your passport What you need Cost
British or Irish Nothing to arrange. None
Any passport, if you live in the UK with permission to stay Nothing to arrange. Bring the passport you live here on. None
United States, Canada, the European Union, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein An Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before you fly. Apply on gov.uk or in the official UK ETA app, never through another website. GBP 20 per person
Ghanaian, living in Ghana A UK Standard Visitor visa. Adansi Travels, our travel partner in Ghana, can guide you. See below . GBP 135 per person
Ghanaian, living in Europe or the Nordics A UK Standard Visitor visa. A residence permit or a Schengen visa does not replace it. Apply on gov.uk , then attend the visa centre where you live for fingerprints and a photograph. GBP 135 per person
Any other passport Check on gov.uk in two minutes. Varies

The style guide
## The art of wearing Kente.
Read it like a map. Every detail has a meaning.
How to wear Kente
## For kings
1 The full cloth One full cloth, woven strip by strip and sewn together. Every pattern has a name and a meaning.
2 Right shoulder bare The cloth passes under the right arm, so the right shoulder stays bare, the way the chiefs wear it.
3 Over the left shoulder The long end is thrown over the left shoulder and falls down the back.
4 Ahenema sandals Royal leather sandals, handmade. With black tie, polished shoes.
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
## For queens
5 The headpiece A gold band or a sculpted duku, tall and proud for the Gala.
6 Beads and gold Krobo beads at the neck, gold at the wrist and the arm. Wear the pieces handed down to you.
7 Two cloths A wrapped cloth to the ankle and an upper cloth across the body, or a kaba and slit in Kente.
8 Jewelled sandals Ahenema or jewelled evening sandals, never trainers.
## How to wrap the cloth, in four moves.
1 Open the cloth Hold the cloth open behind you, the top edge level with your shoulders.
2 Under the right arm Bring the right end under your right arm and across the chest. The right shoulder stays bare.
3 Over the left shoulder Throw the long end over your left shoulder so it falls down your back.
4 Gather and hold Gather the folds over your left arm and hold them in your left hand. Walk slowly, with grace.
Colours and their meaning
## Colours with meaning.
Gold Royalty, wealth and the Gold Coast. The colour of the Gala.
White Joy, purity and victory. A colour of celebration.
Green The forests and the fields of home.
Red, gold and green The flag, worn together. A celebration.
The etiquette of the evening
## Small courtesies. A memorable night.
A few quiet customs that make the Gala feel like the occasion it is.
Arrive on time Doors at 18:30 for 20:00. The last guests are received at 19:45, so that dinner is served to every table together.
Wait for the toast At midnight the hall rises together for the toast to Ghana. Please keep phones away for that moment, and for the reading at 11:00 on Saturday.
Honour the elders Traditional leaders are greeted as Nana, and elders are greeted first.
Kente is worn with respect For men, the cloth is draped over the left shoulder. Choose the colours you love. Every pattern carries a meaning.
Decorations Miniature decorations and orders may be worn with Black Tie, ball gown or Kente.
Leave gracefully Carriages at 00:30. Our hosts will point every guest to a taxi or to the Night Tube at Bank.
Dress code questions
## Before you dress.
Still unsure? Call Asantewaa on +44 7824 555307 and she will help.
Do I have to wear Kente to the Gala?
No. This is a gala dinner and ball. A ball gown, a long evening gown, a dinner jacket or a fugu smock are all perfect. Kente is welcome, never expected.
Can I wear a short dress to the Gala?
The Gala is a long gown evening. Please choose a floor length or ankle length gown, or Kente cloth, rather than a short dress. Black is always welcome.
I am not Ghanaian. Can I wear Kente?
Yes. Kente and Ghanaian cloth are for everyone, worn with respect and joy. New to Kente? Add it when you book and we help you wear it properly.
Can I wear the dress of another African nation?
Yes. Wear your heritage proudly. Agbada, boubou, kitenge and every royal dress of the continent belong at the Gala.
Where can I find Kente in time?
Add Kente and gold when you book and our Kente partners will hold sashes, stoles and accessories for you, ready to collect.
I am in mourning. Can I still come?
Yes, and you are very welcome. Come as you are. Black is always welcome, and so is your mourning cloth. This is a family celebration, and family includes everyone.
What do I wear on my head?
A headwrap or gele is the crown of this event. Keep it clear of the view of the guests behind you.
Is there a cloakroom?
Yes, staffed from the moment doors open on every day.
Will I be refused entry?
We would rather welcome you than turn you away. Please follow the dress code: guests in sportswear at the Gala may be asked to change.

## General
What is Ghana at 70 UK?
The global celebration of the Ghana 70th Platinum Jubilee: three separate events in London, for guests from across the UK, Europe, the Americas and Ghana, each with its own ticket, marking seventy years of Ghanaian independence: the Royal Jubilee Gala on Friday 5 March 2027, the Ghana Day Festival on Saturday 6 March 2027, and Women of the Motherland on Sunday 7 March 2027.
Can I attend if I am not Ghanaian?
Of course. Ghana at 70 UK is for everyone. Guests of every background and every heritage are warmly welcome on all three days.
Can I come to just one day?
Yes. Each day is ticketed separately and is complete on its own.
How is the programme timed?
Every day is planned to a published running order, sent to ticket holders before the event, so you can relax and enjoy it.
Is there a virtual option?
No. Ghana at 70 UK is a celebration held in person.
How do I book?
Choose your event on the Tickets page and book. Bookings are open, only on this website, and prices include all fees.
## Tickets and payment
When can I book?
Now, only on this website. A table of ten is GBP 1,800, ten guests for the price of nine (9 x GBP 200).
Can I get a refund?
No. All sales are final and tickets cannot be refunded. If you cannot attend, transfer your ticket to someone else at no extra cost by emailing us their name before 17:00 on the day before. If we cancel the event, you are refunded in full.
Is there a prize draw?
Yes. Every ticket holder is entered into the Mefie hamper draw, and anyone can enter free, with no purchase, at ghanaat70uk.com/draw. One entry per person, the same chance either way. Entries close at 23:59 on Sunday 28 February 2027, and the winner is drawn on Independence Day, Saturday 6 March 2027.
I am not Ghanaian. Can I come?
Yes, and you are very welcome. Ghana at 70 UK is for everyone, whatever your heritage. Bring your colleagues, neighbours and friends. On Friday guests wear Black Tie, ball gown or Kente, and the dress code page shows how to wear Kente and print with confidence.
I need a UK visa. Where do I start?
Download our free visa and ETA checklist. It takes you step by step: what to gather, what your bank statements must show, ready letters and the online form. Every cost of your trip is yours: Ghana at 70 UK does not sponsor any visa or traveller and is not responsible for any cost. Download the checklist .
I live in Europe or the Nordics on a Ghanaian passport. What do I need?
A UK Standard Visitor visa, GBP 135, even with a residence permit or permanent residence. Apply online from early December 2026, give your fingerprints at the visa application centre where you live, and allow about three weeks. EU, Swiss, Norwegian and Icelandic passport holders need an ETA, GBP 20. Visas and travel .
I live outside the UK. Can I come?
Yes, and we would love you to. Guests are coming from across Europe, North America and Ghana. Book online in GBP from anywhere in the world. Most visitors from Europe and North America need a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before they fly: apply at gov.uk/eta. Visitors from Ghana need a UK visitor visa: see Plan your journey . Our Stay team books hotels near Bank station.
Can I pay by bank transfer?
Yes. Choose bank transfer when you book and we send our account details with your booking reference. Payment must arrive within 24 hours, or the booking is released. Tickets are issued once payment arrives.
Can I add extras or host a private table?
Yes. Once your tickets are paid you can add private parties, celebration packages and portrait packages. Extras are priced on request.
Where should I book?
Only on this website, through the Book now buttons. Tickets bought anywhere else are not valid.
## The Royal Jubilee Gala
What is the dress code?
Black tie and ball gowns, with Kente welcome. Miniature decorations may be worn.
Can I book for a group of ten?
Yes. A table of ten is GBP 1,800: ten guests seated together at the long tables, for the price of nine: 9 x GBP 200. Choose Table of ten when you book.
Are there awards?
No. Ghana at 70 UK is a celebration of Ghana, not an awards night. There are no awards, prizes or judging on any day.
## Ghana Day Festival
Can I bring children?
Yes. All ages are welcome on all three days. Children must be accompanied by an adult at all times, and every guest, adult or child, holds a ticket. The event is held over two floors joined by stairs, so pushchairs and buggies cannot be accommodated.
Is there food and drink?
Saturday is a festival, not a meal. The bar sells drinks and snacks all day, card only. Food is not included in the GBP 50 ticket, and food and drink cannot be brought in. Over 18s only at the bar, and we follow Challenge 25.
Is anything on Saturday evening?
No. The festival closes at 17:00.
## Women of the Motherland
Who is Sunday for?
Every woman, whatever her heritage, with her family and friends. Mothers, fathers, sons, daughters and grandparents are all welcome at family tables.
Does everyone pay the same?
Yes. GBP 150 per guest covers afternoon tea, the Wall of Mothers, the toolkit, a family portrait and the networking hour, whether or not you drink alcohol.
Is there an age limit?
All ages welcome, as on every day. Children accompanied by an adult at all times. Every guest needs a ticket.
Is there more than one sitting?
No. There is one sitting and the whole room is together all day. Doors open at 11:00 and we close at 18:30.

Where is the venue?
All three days are at Banking Hall, 14 Cornhill, London EC3V 3ND, in the City of London, moments from the Bank of England.
I do not live in London. Can you arrange my stay?
Yes. We book a hotel close to the venue or within your budget, plus airport and station transfers. Send a request from the Plan your journey page and receive your options within one working day.
Is the venue accessible?
Banking Hall is a historic building and the event is held over two floors connected by stairs only, so the event may not be suitable for guests who cannot use stairs. Please call us before booking and we will tell you honestly what is possible. See the access guide .

# Page: https://ghanaat70uk.com/about
Our story Freedom and Justice
## The Ghana Platinum Jubilee.
On 6 March 1957 the Black Star rose over an independent Ghana. On 6 March 2027 the nation reaches seventy years, its Platinum Jubilee, and everyone who loves Ghana, from across the world, will celebrate it in style, with three days in London. Meet the founders .
The story The jubilee The founders The nation The symbol The flag The diaspora Book The three days
1957 · 2027 · Seventy years
## A Platinum Jubilee for the Motherland.
At midnight on 6 March 1957, tens of thousands stood under the warm night sky of Accra and waited.
Then Kwame Nkrumah spoke the words a continent had waited a lifetime to hear: “Ghana, your beloved country, is free forever.” The crowds celebrated through the night. That morning the Duchess of Kent, representing the Queen, read her message to the new nation: “The hopes of many, especially in Africa, hang on your endeavours.”
Ghana carried those hopes. Ghana carries them still.
Continue the story
Seventy years on, the children of that midnight are everywhere, from London and Milton Keynes to Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds, Glasgow, Cardiff, Belfast and Dublin, from Amsterdam and Hamburg to New York, Houston and Toronto, and home in Accra and Kumasi. Our parents arrived with a suitcase, a winter coat that was never quite warm enough and an extraordinary amount of courage. They worked the night shifts, studied after long days, filled the church halls on Sunday and sent money home on Friday. They built careers, businesses and families, and they raised us to know exactly where we come from.
We have never forgotten home.
Some of us were born in Kumasi, some in Lewisham, in Manchester or in Milton Keynes. Some of us speak Twi, Ga, Ewe, Fante or Dagbani. Some of us only understand it when our mothers are angry.
Every one of us carries a Ghana of our own: waakye on a Saturday morning, a grandmother calling us by our day name, the first highlife record at a family party, the cousin who taught us to dance Azonto. And every one of us knows the words of that midnight.
That is why our symbol is Akoko Nan, the leg of the hen. An Akan proverb says the hen treads on her chicks, but she does not kill them. It is the love of a mother who shelters and corrects, firm and gentle at once, and never lets go. Its two curls are the chicks held close, its crescent the line that shields them, and its point faces forward, because a mother meets danger before it reaches her children. Gold for the Gold Coast, green for the land.
Ghana is ours, and we are Ghana. The Motherland is us.
Seventy years is a platinum jubilee. In June 2022 Britain showed the world how such a milestone is honoured. For Queen Elizabeth II, the first British monarch to reign for seventy years, the nation gave a four day bank holiday weekend, from 2 to 5 June. More than 3,500 beacons blazed across the UK and the Commonwealth. A Service of Thanksgiving was held in the City of London. Streets became banqueting halls, with more than 85,000 Big Jubilee Lunches, and some 10,000 people carried the Platinum Jubilee Pageant past Buckingham Palace.
Now it is the turn of Ghana.
The two stories were always joined. Elizabeth II came to the throne in 1952. Five years into her reign, Ghana became independent with her as Queen of Ghana, until the nation declared itself a Republic on 1 July 1960. In November 1961 she came to Accra as the guest of President Kwame Nkrumah, and the two danced together at the farewell ball, a moment still remembered in both countries.
On 6 March 2027 Ghana reaches a Platinum Jubilee of its own: seventy years as a sovereign nation. It deserves the same ceremony, the same pride and the same joyful noise. So guests from across the UK, Europe, the Americas and Ghana will gather in one great hall, Banking Hall in the City of London, moments from the Bank of England, for Ghana at 70 UK, The Platinum Jubilee Celebrations.
## Britain gave the Queen four days. We give Ghana three.
The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 A four day bank holiday weekend Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027 Three days at Banking Hall, 5 to 7 March
The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 Beacons lit across the land Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027 The midnight toast as Independence Day begins
The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 The Platinum Party at the Palace Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027 The Royal Jubilee Gala, a Ghanaian inspired dinner and a ball
The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 The Big Jubilee Lunch in every street Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027 The Ghana Day Festival for the whole community
The UK Platinum Jubilee, June 2022 The Platinum Jubilee Pageant Ghana at 70 UK, Platinum Jubilee, 6 March 2027 The runway and the drums
A platinum jubilee asks two questions: what have these seventy years given us, and what will we give the next seventy? We gather to honour the Ghana we came from, to shape the one our children will inherit, and to lift one another while we do it.
For those who came before us. For those who walk beside us. For those who will follow.
Three days. One people. One Platinum Jubilee.
Take your seat at the Platinum Jubilee Partner with us
Sources: contemporary reports of 6 March 1957, published records of the Platinum Jubilee weekend of 2 to 5 June 2022, and histories of the 1961 state visit to Ghana.
The meaning
## What is a platinum jubilee?
A jubilee is a great anniversary, kept with ceremony, thanksgiving and joy. Each has its own name, and seventy years has the finest of all: platinum.
Silver 25 years 1982
Golden 50 years 2007
Diamond 60 years 2017
Sapphire 65 years 2022
Platinum 70 years 6 March 2027
The meaning, in full
## The sound of the horn
The word jubilee comes from the ancient Hebrew yobel , the horn of a ram. In the old law, a horn was sounded every fiftieth year to open a year of restoration: land returned to its families, debts were set aside, and those held in bondage were released.
“Proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof.” Leviticus 25:10
For a nation that lit the way to independence for a continent, no word could be more fitting. A jubilee was always a celebration of liberty, of homecoming and of a people restored to themselves.
## What a platinum jubilee asks of us
Give thanks. For seventy years of nationhood, and for everyone who paid for it.
Remember. The names, the sacrifices and the songs, so that our children know them by heart.
Come together. Every region, every faith and every generation, in one hall, across three days.
Look ahead. To the Ghana of the next seventy years, which we will help to build.
## Our Platinum Jubilee
Seventy years ago a people stood together at midnight and claimed their future. Seventy years on, we honour every generation that carried the Black Star forward: the farmers and the teachers, the nurses and the soldiers, the market women and the scholars, and the mothers and fathers who crossed the sea so that their children could stand tall in Britain.
This is our seventy years of service, of sacrifice and of faith. It deserves its own beacon, its own feast and its own pageant, in the heart of London, in our finest cloth.
Sound the horn. Light the beacon. Lay the table. Seventy years of Ghana.
Sources: World Wide Words on the history of the word jubilee, and Leviticus 25 in the King James Version.
Who we are
## We build rooms where everyone is honoured.
Ghana at 70 UK is made by two joint founders, Asantewaa and Adwoa, who have spent their working lives bringing the diaspora together, across the UK, in Accra and everywhere in between.
Every year on 6 March, Ghana celebrates the night it stood before the world and lit the way for a continent. For the seventieth, we are bringing that night to London for the whole world: three days, one great hall, and a welcome for every family of the Motherland, wherever on earth they live.
We are not a committee and we are not a brand. We are daughters of the Motherland who believe every guest deserves the finest room in the country, and the warmest welcome in it.
Together they opened the new Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. Together they founded Accra Konnect. Together they bring you Ghana at 70 UK.
Joint founder · Venue, sponsorship and production
## Asantewaa-Gloria Ayim
Joint founder of Accra Konnect, and together with Adwoa opened the new Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. Twenty years delivering events at the highest level, for Pirelli, the Spanish national football team and Champions League clubs.
She builds the room.
Joint founder · Exhibitors, partnerships and dignitaries
## Adwoa Agyemang
Joint founder of Accra Konnect, and together with Asantewaa opened the new Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. Founded Ghanaian Londoners Network in 2009 and has delivered over thirty community events since. Created the Women in Enterprise Awards, spent nine years in PR and media in Accra, and sits on the Ghana Nigeria Business Council Executive Committee.
She fills it with people.
A message from Asantewaa and Adwoa
Four years ago we opened the new Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. We saw what it means to our people to be received with dignity, in a room made for them. That is what we are building again.
A platinum jubilee is not an anniversary. It is a homecoming. Our parents crossed oceans so that we could stand tall in this city, and in March we will stand together, in Kente and in our Sunday best, in one of the most beautiful halls in London.
Bring your mother. Bring your children. Bring the friend who has never been. There is a seat at our table for every one of you.
Asantewaa and Adwoa Asantewaa-Gloria Ayim and Adwoa Agyemang, joint founders

A national occasion
## Kept with the dignity the nation deserves.
Seventy years of sovereignty is a moment for the whole nation, at home and abroad. Ghana at 70 UK marks it in London with ceremony, with care for every generation and with a clear purpose: to honour where we came from and to strengthen the bond between Ghana and its people in Britain.
Ceremony The midnight toast on Independence Eve, and at 11:00 on Independence Day the drums and a reading of the declaration of independence, seventy years to the day.
Heritage The flag of Theodosia Okoh, the Black Star and the true stories of Ghanaians in Britain since 1555, on the Heritage Wall for all three days.
The diaspora at work Practical talks on land, money, wills, pensions and business, for families who build their lives between Britain and Ghana.
Every generation Elders honoured, mothers celebrated on Mothering Sunday, and young Ghanaians born in Britain given a place at the heart of the day.
Created by the team that produced the opening of the Ghana Passport Office in Aldgate East. Official, diplomatic and institutional delegations are welcome, with protocol and seating arranged with each delegation. Official enquiries
Akoko Nan · the leg of the hen
The symbol, explained
The symbol
## The mother who protects.
Our symbol is Akoko Nan, an Adinkra symbol carried by an Akan proverb: Akoko nan tia ba, na enkum ba . The hen treads on her chicks, but she does not kill them.
It is the love of a mother who shelters her children and corrects them, but never harms them. Firm and gentle at once. At seventy, Ghana is that mother. Her children are everywhere, in London and Manchester, in Hamburg and Amsterdam, in New York and at home in Accra, and however far we travel, she keeps us close.
The two curls The chicks, held close, one above and one below.
The crescent The strong outer line that shields them.
The point Facing forward. A mother meets danger before it reaches her children.
Gold and green Gold for the Gold Coast, the name the land carried before 1957. Green for the land of the Motherland.
Why a mother. The Platinum Jubilee opens on Independence Eve and closes on Mothering Sunday: the celebration of a nation that ends with a celebration of the women who carried it. No other symbol would do.
The flag and the symbol. The flag belongs to the nation. The symbol belongs to the family. Red, gold and green fly for Ghana. Gold and green, with Akoko Nan, mark this gathering of her children.
The wordmark. GHANA AT 70 UK is set in wide, classical capitals beneath the symbol, with the line The Platinum Jubilee Celebrations, so the name reads with the calm of an engraved invitation. Akoko Nan is also cast as the Jubilee pin, in solid brass plated in 24 carat gold.
Theodosia Salome Okoh · 1922 to 2015
Her story, in full
The woman who designed the flag
## Theodosia Okoh.
Every flag raised at Ghana at 70 UK began on the drawing board of one woman. Theodosia Salome Okoh, an artist trained at Achimota School, designed the flag of Ghana, flown for the first time at independence on 6 March 1957.
Born in Effiduase on 13 June 1922, she answered the call for a flag for the new nation, and her design was adopted by Kwame Nkrumah. She went on to become the first woman to chair the Ghana Hockey Association, led the sport for more than twenty years, and saw Ghana reach its first Hockey World Cup and Olympic Games. The National Hockey Stadium in Accra bears her name. She died in 2015, aged 92, and was honoured with a state funeral.
Red For those who gave their lives and their labour for independence.
Gold For the mineral wealth of the land.
Green For the forests and the rich vegetation.
The Black Star For African freedom and unity, the lodestar of a continent.
On Mothering Sunday, Women of the Motherland honours the women who carried Ghana. Theodosia Okoh gave it the colours we wear.
Before 1957
## Our diaspora story.
Long before independence, our people were crossing oceans to Britain: princes and priests, scholars and sprinters, lawyers, soldiers and the students who would lead a nation to independence. These are some of those who came before us.
Read the ten stories
1555
## Shama to London
Five men from Shama, on the Gold Coast, come to London to learn English for the gold trade. Nearly five centuries of Ghanaians in Britain begin.
1749
## The Royal African
William Ansah Sessarakoo of Anomabu, sold into slavery and freed, arrives in London as a guest of the Earl of Halifax. His portrait, painted and engraved in London, survives to this day.
1754
## A boy from Cape Coast
Philip Quaque leaves Cape Coast to study in England. In 1765 he becomes the first African ordained in the Church of England.
1882
## The fastest man in Britain
Arthur Wharton of Jamestown, Accra, arrives in England. In 1886 he equals the 100 yards world record, then becomes the first Black professional footballer in the world.
1896
## A lawyer for a nation
J. E. Casely Hayford is called to the Bar in London, and later writes one of the first novels in English by an African.
1925
## Africa in Camden
The West African Students Union is founded in London, with J. B. Danquah its first president. Its Africa House becomes a home from home.
1927
## The doctor of philosophy
J. B. Danquah becomes the first West African to earn a doctorate from a British university.
1945
## Burghley Road, Kentish Town
Kwame Nkrumah rents a room at 60 Burghley Road, Kentish Town, and helps organise the Fifth Pan African Congress. A blue plaque marks the house.
1948
## The soldiers who came home
Veterans of the Gold Coast Regiment, marching for promised benefits, are fired on in Accra. Their deaths set the nation on the road to freedom.
1957
## Independence, and the journey continues
Ghana is independent, under a flag of red, gold and green designed by Theodosia Okoh. At the 2021 census, 132,577 people born in Ghana lived in England and Wales.
All ten stories stand on the Heritage Wall at Banking Hall across the three days, so every guest walks past the people who came before them. Partner a story .
Sources: London Museum, English Heritage, the Inner Temple, the Office for National Statistics 2021 census and published histories.
